senses.gloss: f. (b. h.) Hebrew; (לשין) ע׳ Hebrew language; (כתב) ע׳ Hebrew character, type.
units: <cite ref="Mishnah Kiddushin 1:2">Kidd. I, 2</cite> <he>עבד ע׳</he> a Hebrew slave; <he>אמה הע׳</he> a Hebrew handmaid.
<cite ref="Bereishit Rabbah 42:8">Gen. R. s. 42</cite> <he>ומשיח בלשון ע׳</he>, v. <cite ref="P00062"><he>עֵבֶר</he> II</cite>.
<cite ref="Mishnah Gittin 9:6">Gitt. IX, 6</cite> <he>עד אחד עברי וכ׳</he> if one witness signed in Hebrew type, and the other in Greek, and again one in Hebrew &c.
<cite ref="Mishnah Gittin 9:8">Ib. 8</cite> <he>גט שכתבו עברית וכ׳</he> if a letter of divorce was written in Hebrew, and its witnesses signed in Greek.

<cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Megillah 1:9:3">Y. Meg. I, 71ᵇ</cite> bot.; <cite ref="Esther Rabbah 4:12">Esth. R. to I, 22</cite>, a. e. <he>ע׳ לדיבור</he> the Hebrew language is adapted for oratory; a. fr.—

<cite ref="Megillah 18a:20">Meg. 18ᵃ</cite> <he>קראה … עברית</he> if he read the Megillah in a trans-Euphratean (Aramaic) translation.—Pl. <cite ref="P00071"><he>עִבְרִים</he></cite>, <he>עִבְרִיִּים</he>; f. <cite ref="P00168"><he>עִבְרִיּוֹת</he></cite>.
<cite ref="Megillah 18a:20">Ib.</cite> <he>עברית לע׳</he> an Aramaic translation read before Aramæan Jews.
Ex. R. s. 3 למה קורא אותם ע׳ על שם שעברו ים why does he call them ‘Ibriim (Ex. III, 18)? Because they passed the sea (on going to Egypt).
<cite ref="Pesikta Rabbati 23:1">Pesik. R. s. 23</cite>; a. fr.
